body.x: [Las Vegas, U.S. = Aving News] AI FOR PET (CEO Euna Huh) announced that they participated in CES 2023 held in Las Vegas, U.S. for four days from Thursday, January 5 to Sunday, January 8, 2023 in local time.

Founded in 2020, AI FOR PET launched TTCare, its pet healthcare app service powered by AI and data analysis technology, in January 2021. TTCare was the first app to be licensed as “Medical Imaging Assistant Software for Veterinary Medical Devices” by the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency in recognition of its accuracy in AI analysis. It was selected as a winner in the CES 2022 and 2023 Innovation Awards and also chosen as part of Forbes Asia 100 To Watch 2022.

TTCare is an AI-based total healthcare app service for pets that uses AI to inform users if there are signs of disease-related abnormalities in the areas where they took pictures with their phones — such as pets' eyes and skin. This technology related to checking eye and skin health has been patented in South Korea, and three patent applications have been filed abroad. In addition, the solution provides various information necessary for health care in consideration of the type and age of pets.

As an expert in big data analysis with AI, AI FOR PET’s CEO Eun-ah Heo said that she has always thought about how AI technology can create innovation even in everyday life, and has always wanted to be able to check the health of her pets — her lifelong companions — anytime and anywhere. Based on their experiences and insights, all members of AI FOR PET held the ideal of creating a world where pet owners can manage and maintain their pet’s health in any situation, which led to the development of the TTCare service.

The inception of TTCare was also inspired by a paper titled “CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) based diagnosis models for canine ulcerative keratitis,” which was published in the journal Scientific Reports in 2019. At the time of launch, over 500,000 samples of pet image data were used to train AI models, which have now learned over 2 million datasets to identify signs of various diseases more accurately.

body.cap: Demonstration of TTCare │Photo by Aving News

body.x: Since the launch of the Android version in January 2021 and the iOS version in March, about 130,000 pet owners have signed up to become members of TTCare, checking their pets’ eye and skin health over 450,000 times. Encouraged by the positive response from the users, AI FOR PET is putting more effort in development and collaboration to provide more diverse and convenient services in the future.

According to a representative from AI FOR PET, “We launched a service to enable contact-free consultation with veterinarians, nutritionists, and trainers in Korea. Also, we are engaged in ongoing discussions with businesses and veterinary hospitals/clinics in the United States for partnerships. During the first half of 2023, video-based joint exams and photo-based dental check-ups will also be updated.”

The representative added that “The U.S. version of the service launched in June 2022 began pilot operation in two Californian hospitals in January 2023 to try the app in different ways, and we are in talks about pilot operation with three other hospitals. In the United States, it takes about one or two months to get check-ups, and veterinarians are often exhausted due to their overwhelming workloads. We hope that TTCare can realize improvements in the pet-caring environment in the future.”

body.cap: AI FOR PET has been honored in the CES Innovation Awards for two consecutive years for TTCare. │Photo by Aving News

body.x: Aspiring to go beyond their current achievements, the firm is going to launch the German service in February while having ongoing discussions for service launches and collaboration in Japan and Italy. “At CES 2023, feed corporations from the United States and Canada showed keen interest in our technology, and we have been discussing how to provide our service to them. A veterinary hospital in Nevada and another to open in New York have also shown interest in utilizing TTCare. Also, various domestic and foreign investors have requested data, and we had about 17 meetings related to investment and partnership,” explained the representative.

Meanwhile, TTCare service is supported by big data and artificial intelligence (AI) technology. AI learning requires a large amount of various data to be accumulated. In addition to the data collected on its own, AI FOR PET was able to enhance the performance of their existing AI models by utilizing publicly accessible AI learning data through AI-Hub established by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National Information Society Agency.

Organized by the Ministry of Science and ICT and promoted by the National Information Society Agency, the data building project for AI learning which has built a total of 1,300 types of data, will remain open to the public via AI-Hub until 2025. This project has addressed the difficulty in data building, which typically has high costs in terms of time and money, driving the growth of AI SMEs and startups in Korea. AI learning data can be accessed and downloaded by the public on the AI-Hub website.
